title: Temperature
what: The surface coloured by its temperature, or over the last 800,000 years by its change from today, and each model’s mean.
how: Over the last 800,000 years, Krapp et al. (2021): annual mean temperature on land every 1,000 years, of which the site keeps every other, a statistical emulator of 72 HadCM3 climate-model runs driven by CO₂, Earth’s orbit and the ice sheets, averaged by the site to a 1° grid; the sea and the ice sheets have none and keep their relief colours. Its maps are on today’s geography, so a place can be set beside itself today: by default the colours show that change, blue colder and red warmer; within about a degree of today the land is left uncoloured, so a scale's pale middle is not taken for ice. Krapp et al.'s present is pre-industrial, so from 1850 on the chart beside the globe, and at today on any scale, the globe shows the measured warming instead: Berkeley Earth's 5-year means on land and sea, as the change from 1850–1900. Further back, maps every 5 million years, packed into images and blended between them.
others: Krapp et al. is a model emulator, not proxy measurements: the ice cores and reconstructions in the boundaries story’s Holocene chapter are the measured side. Its mean is over ice-free land only, and a different land at each moment: at an ice age's height the ice-covered land is left out and the bared shelves come in, so the mean understates the cold (about 4 °C below today at the last glacial maximum, where places by the ice were near 20 °C colder) and cannot be set beside the others' global means. Scotese 2022 and CESM (Li et al. 2023) disagree, at times by several degrees: pick whose to colour by.
